I am 39 years old, I finished primary school and have been farming our land in Quzhou since I was a teenager. My family has about 8 mu of flat, irrigated land here on the North China Plain. Around here, everyone follows the winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping system — it is what our land and climate are made for, and it is how we feed our family and earn cash.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed an improved variety, luyuan502, about 35 jin per mu, after rotary tillage to break up the stubble from the previous maize crop. Right now, at the start of the growing season, I am watching the wheat green up. I will topdress with urea at jointing stage and irrigate three times total: once now at green-up or jointing, once at heading if the weather turns dry, and once at grain filling. Weeds are already showing, so I will spray herbicide once. I also watch for aphids and powdery mildew — I will spray insecticide twice and fungicide once. I put down compound fertilizer as basal dressing in autumn, and that plus the spring urea gives me roughly what I need.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant maize the same day or the next. I do not till for maize — I sow directly into the wheat stubble to save diesel and time, just like my neighbors. I will plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed, one package per mu from the local shop. Basal compound fertilizer goes down at sowing, and I will irrigate twice: once at seedling stage and once at filling. One herbicide spray and two insecticide sprays for corn borer are enough — I usually do not bother with fungicide on maize.

I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and about 550 kg per mu from the maize. That is enough to keep grain for the family and sell the rest.
